subject: Medford High School Graduation and Competency Policy
overview: The School Committee updated graduation requirements to align with the removal of the MCAS graduation mandate and authorized a feasibility study agreement for the high school building project.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved routine business including payroll, grants, meeting minutes, and donations for musical instruments and staff development.

items.title: Winter Guard Field Trip
items.summary: Approved a trip for the Winter Guard to attend a national competition in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania.

items.title: MHS Graduation and Competency Requirements
items.summary: Approved a first reading of updated graduation requirements that replace the MCAS competency determination with successful completion of aligned coursework in English, math, and science. Interim Superintendent Suzanne Galusi clarified that while MCAS scores will no longer determine graduation, student participation remains mandatory for district accountability ratings.

items.title: Summer Fun Program Fees
items.summary: Set a tiered fee structure for the Summer Fun program, establishing rates of $200 for students with financial need, $250 for residents, and $300 for non-residents. The committee moved to formalize these rates to ensure transparency and accountability instead of relying on informal scholarship requests.

items.title: Field Trip Financial Support Policy
items.summary: Referred a proposal to develop a formal policy regarding district financial support for local and out-of-state field trips to the Rules and Policy Subcommittee.

items.title: High School Building Committee Membership
items.summary: Approved membership updates for the building committee, including replacing the former superintendent with the interim superintendent and extending the committee's term through September 2026.

items.title: MSBA Feasibility Study Agreement
items.summary: Authorized the district to enter into a feasibility study agreement with the Massachusetts School Building Authority for the Medford High School project. The agreement follows the certification of a future enrollment target of 1,395 students.
